Summary: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints was founded by Joseph Smith in the United States in 1830. It is included here as a modern comparison entry because its teachings on God, Christ, and Scripture differ from historic Nicene Christianity, while its members describe themselves as Christians.
Beliefs: God the Father has a physical body and was once mortal in Latter-day Saint teaching; Additional Scriptures include the Book of Mormon; Continuing revelation comes through a living prophet; Humans can progress toward exaltation
Controversy: Discussed in comparative theology since the 19th century; historic churches note differences from the Nicene Creed on God and Christ
ChristianResponse: Historic churches respond by affirming the Trinity as defined at Nicaea and the sufficiency of the biblical canon, citing Deuteronomy and Revelation on adding to Scripture, while encouraging respectful dialogue.
